info.name: Central RBAC: Keycloak, IAM registries and Frappe services
info.description: Manual versions of the calls central-rbac will automate: create users, roles and user-role mappings in Keycloak; role, permission and role-permission catalogue in the IAM staff portal; Frappe roles and doctype permissions; DA scoped assignments. Fill the environment before running.

item.name: 0. Quick start: create client, role and user in the realm
item.description: Needs only kc_admin_password in the environment. Uses the default test names below; change them before running against a shared realm. 'Create' leaves the objects in place; run 'Cleanup' to remove them.

request.description: 201 with a Location header ending in the client's internal UUID. 409 means the clientId already exists.

item.name: 1. IAM staff portal (registry role + permission catalogue)
item.description: Roles and permissions live in the IAM database; the Keycloak client role of the same mnemonic is what puts the role in the user's token. All calls are POST with the G2P envelope and a CSRF double-submit pair (the collection pre-request script sets both).

item.name: Login through IAM (same flow the UI uses)

request.description: Public. Note the id of the staff provider and put it in iam_login_provider_id.
Returns the identity provider's authorization URL and a state value.
Keycloak keeps its session in cookies, so run L3 to L5 together in one run (Postman and newman keep the cookie jar).
Keycloak answers 302 with the IAM callback URL (it carries the authorization code).
IAM exchanges the code and sets X-Access-Token as a cookie. The script reads it and stores it as iam_token.

exec: // IAM sets its own double-submit CSRF cookie at login; later calls must echo that value in X-CSRF-Token

request.description: Shows client_roles. The caller needs IAM_ADMIN under client_roles['iam-staff-ui'] for the calls below.
Find the application_id for the registry (one of the registered mnemonics).
There is no update_role route, so a role cannot be renamed here: create the new one, move mappings, delete the old one.

item.name: 2. Service admin API (oan_auth_service wrappers on any oan_* site)
item.description: Wrappers in oan_auth_service (api/v1/admin.py): no raw Frappe methods, no API key. Set service_base_url to the gateway host of the service, fill service_admin_user and service_admin_password, then run '0. Login' and the quick start. Roles and doctypes are limited to the site's service prefix.

request.description: Local login of a user holding System Manager or Administrator on that site (the admin routes require it). Sets app_jwt, used by this folder and by folder 3. Rate limited to 30 per minute.

item.name: Quick start: onboard a user (run in order)
1. List roles of this service (picks the test roles)

request.description: Read only. Picks a non-admin role as service_role, and a second one as service_role_2. Set service_role_name in the environment to force a role. A 400 'No service prefix is configured' means the site has no oan_service_prefix hook or service_prefix config.

exec: const names = (d || []).map(r => typeof r === 'string' ? r : (r.name || r.role)).filter(Boolean);
console.log('roles:', names.join(', '), '| using', pm.environment.get('service_role'), '/', second || '(no second role)');

request.description: Creates a throw-away account with a unique email per run. There is no delete route, so cleanup disables it.
Skipped when the service has only one non-admin role.

item.name: User permissions: restrict the quick-start user to one record (run after the quick start, before Cleanup)

request.description: Limits the user to one record (`restrict_value`) of a service doctype (`restrict_doctype`). Skipped until both are set in the environment. Needs the gateway route for POST /v1/admin/users/:user_id/user-permissions.
Restrictions of the user on this service's doctypes only.
Deletes the restriction added in step 1.

item.name: Cleanup (disables, then deletes the test user)

request.description: Disables the test user. The next step deletes it.

item.name: Roles: create, disable and delete a test role (run in order)
Reference: list users and permissions (read only)

request.description: Drop either query parameter to list more. if_owner rules are listed but cannot be edited here.

item.name: Permissions: changes the site's rules (run deliberately, not part of the quick start)

request.description: true grants a right, false revokes it. The first change to a doctype copies ALL its standard rules into custom rules; from then on the app's DocType JSON no longer applies on migrate until the doctype is reset.

item.name: Remove a role's rule on a doctype

request.description: Deletes every custom rule of the doctype, for all roles. Destructive.

item.name: 3. DA Services scoped role assignments
item.description: Paths follow da_services/api/v1/rbac.py. These take a JWT (app_jwt): run folder 2, request 0 (Login), first.

request.description: The Frappe User must already exist. Scope fields are optional; the role's scope type decides which are used.
